## 1. Introduction

SairFramework (SFW for short) is a **multi-component interaction platform written in Java**. Its goal is to **eliminate useless redundancy**:

- One unified Swing console hosts every functional component instead of one program per tiny tool;
- **Plain-text IR scripts** (`.ir`) drive components, editable in Notepad;
- **Plugins (Activity)** add functionality and can be loaded, unloaded or replaced at runtime without restarting the framework;
- A **unified class-loader hierarchy plus built-in toolkits** let plugins share dependencies while staying isolated from each other.

It is both a *runtime* and a *development framework*: `SFW.jar` can be launched directly with `java -jar`, or imported as a dependency into your own Java project (see [Plugin Development](#6-plugin-development-guide)).

---

## 2. Core Features

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| 🔌 Hot-pluggable plugins | Drop a jar into `plugins/exection/` and it is discovered; `uninstall` releases the jar handle at runtime |
| 📜 IR script driven | `.ir` scripts run line by line, with comments, label jumps, variables and embedded commands |
| 🖥 Swing console | Borderless dark console with colored output, background images, tabs, and a system tray icon |
| 🔄 Cross-platform | Windows / Linux / macOS and any Java-capable OS, Java 8+ |
| 🧰 Shared library dir | `plugins/lib/` is loaded by the global `SairLoader` and supports SPI (ServiceLoader / JDBC drivers / audio codecs) and hot unload |
| 🧩 Class isolation | Every plugin gets its own `ExectionLoader`, so identically named classes do not clash |
| 🀄 Chinese support | Chinese package/class/file names work natively; a Chinese component support jar enables fully Chinese coding |
| 🖨 Print proxy | Intercept console output through `PrintRunnable` for logging or forwarding |
| ⚙ Variables & aliases | `/var-add` variables and `oset` aliases can be reused in scripts |

## 3. Quick Start (Deploy & Run)

### 3.1 Requirements

| Item | Requirement |
|---|---|
| OS | Windows, Linux, macOS, and any Java-capable system |
| Java | **Java 8 or newer** (JDK 8 recommended; the release ships a Windows JRE under `8x64/`) |
| Disk | About 300 MB for the full release (including the bundled JRE; about 30 MB without it) |

> `8x64/` is a Windows x64 JRE. If you prefer a system JVM, delete that folder and launch with `java -jar SFW.jar`.

### 3.2 Get the release

- Gitee Releases: <https://gitee.com/sair520/sairframework/releases> (`LatestVersion.zip` / `LatestVersion.tar.gz`)
- Or build it yourself — see [8. Source Layout & Build](#8-source-layout--build)

### 3.3 Runtime directory layout

```text
SairFrameWork/
├─ SFW.jar                 # framework entry (sair.Main)
├─ run.bat                 # Windows launcher (uses the bundled JRE)
├─ run.sh                  # Linux / macOS launcher
├─ 8x64/                   # bundled Windows x64 JRE (optional)
├─ plugins/
│  ├─ lib/                 # shared dependencies (third-party jars)
│  └─ exection/            # plugin jars
├─ data/                   # per-component data directories (auto-created)
│  └─ framework/           # framework data: autorun.ir, BG.jpg, HelloWorld.ir, ...
├─ readme/                 # static documentation site (index.html)
└─ source_code/            # source snapshots (optional)
```

### 3.4 Launch

**Windows**

```bat
:: Option 1: double-click run.bat (uses 8x64\bin\javaw, no console window)
:: Option 2: from a terminal
java -jar SFW.jar
```

**Linux / macOS**

```bash
chmod +x run.sh
./run.sh
# or
java -jar SFW.jar
```

**Launch with an IR script** (autorun.ir runs first, then the given script):

```bash
java -jar SFW.jar "/path/to/script.ir"
```

**Associating .ir files (Windows)**

1. Right-click any `.ir` file → Open with → choose `run.bat` → check "Always use this app";
2. Double-clicking an `.ir` file will then start a new SFW process and run that script.

> SFW is **not a singleton**. Every double-click of an `.ir` file starts a brand-new SFW process.

### 3.5 First run

The console prints version info, Java environment, `lib` load logs and `exection` plugin load logs, then executes `data/framework/autorun.ir` (created empty if missing).

Type `/help` to list all built-in commands, and `/list` to list loaded plugins.

## 4. Console Command Reference

There are two kinds of commands:

- **Framework commands**: start with `/`, e.g. `/list`, `/print hello`;
- **Plugin commands**: `plugin/function args`, e.g. `myplugin/greet World`.

> Format: `plugin/function args`. The part before `/` is the component name; from `/` to the first space is the function name; everything after the first space is passed verbatim to the plugin.
> Wrap path arguments in **double quotes**; single quotes are for **embedded commands**.

### 4.1 Common commands (available on every component)

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `/help` | Show help for the current component |
| `/exit` | Invoke the component's `exit()` hook (the framework does not force the process to quit) |
| `/uninstall` | Unload the current plugin and release its jar handle (framework-level uninstall) |
| `/info` | Show the component's data directory and jar path |
| `/ofunc '[cmd]'` | Execute the quoted command first, then pass its return value to `o_funcMain()` |
| `/oset new old` | Create an alias for a function |
| `/orem alias` | Remove an alias |
| `/close`, `/open` | Temporarily disable / re-enable command input for the component (it stays in memory) |

### 4.2 Console commands (framework component)

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `/clear` | Clear the console |
| `/print [text]` | Print text |
| `/print-c R G B [text]` | Print in color (RGB 0-255) |
| `/println [text]` | Print with a newline |
| `/println-c R G B [text]` | Colored print with a newline |
| `/deprint start len` | Delete a range from the console (`/deprint max max` clears everything) |
| `/print-f "image path"` | Print an image (local file only) |
| `/print-ti` | Print environment info (Java version, paths, ...) |
| `/print-cpr [name]` | Clear a third-party output proxy (empty clears all) |
| `/setBG "image path"` | Set the console background image |
| `/setBC R G B` | Set the background color |
| `/setFC R G B` | Set the default foreground color |
| `/setFCM target R G B` | Set a themed color: `ui-error` / `ex-help` / `ex-info` / `ex` / `mod` |
| `/opacity 10-100` | Set window opacity (100 = fully opaque) |
| `/hide`, `/show` | Hide / show the console window |
| `/resize W H` | Resize the window (no args restores the default) |
| `/list` | List loaded plugins |
| `/list-s` | List plugins in detail (including jar paths) |
| `/load "path or URL"` | Load a plugin jar at runtime (local path / `http(s)://` / `file:`) |
| `/rename old new` | Temporarily rename a plugin (lost on restart) |
| `/ir "path"` | Run an IR script on a new thread |
| `/ir-i "path"` | Run an IR script on the current thread (blocks) |
| `/ir-x name` | Stop the given IR script |
| `/setspliter class` | Switch the command parser (must extend `sair.user.SpliterSPI`) |
| `/var-add name value` | Define a variable, referenced as `%name%` |
| `/var-del name` | Delete a variable |
| `/var-list` | List all variables |
| `/sleep ms` | Sleep the thread |
| `/newthread [cmd]` | Run a command on a separate thread (no thread pool) |

## 5. IR Scripting

IR is SFW's batch execution script: `.ir` suffix, **UTF-8 plain text**, one SFW command per line, executed in order.

### 5.1 Basic syntax

```text
// Lines starting with // are comments; empty lines are ignored

/print-c 0 255 0 Welcome to SairFramework!
/sleep 1000
/println Initializing plugins...
myplugin/hello
myplugin/greet IR user
```

### 5.2 Variables

```text
/var-add myPath D:\Test
/print %myPath%
```

Variables are written by `/var-add` and referenced as `%name%`; scripts and manual input share the same table (`ToolPack.getVmap()`).

### 5.3 Labels and jumps

Define a block with `name {`, close it with `}`, and jump with `/TO:name` (nesting supported, max depth 128 to stop runaway recursion):

```text
loop {
    /println looping...
    /sleep 500
    /TO:loop
}

/TO:loop
```

### 5.4 Embedded commands

Wrap a command in single quotes; its return value replaces the text:

```text
/println 'pl/getNowPlayID'
```

### 5.5 autorun.ir and launch arguments

- On startup, `data/framework/autorun.ir` is **always executed first** (auto-created if missing);
- If an external `.ir` path is passed on the command line (or by double-click), it runs **after** autorun.ir has fully finished.

## 6. Plugin Development Guide

### 6.1 What is a plugin

A plugin is a plain JAR that:

- contains at least one class extending `sair.user.Activity`;
- declares its entry class in `META-INF/MANIFEST.MF` via `ACT`;
- is placed in `plugins/exection/` and discovered on startup;
- is class-isolated from other plugins while being able to reference shared libs in `plugins/lib/`.

### 6.2 Minimal example

```java
package sair.myplugin;

import sair.FCM;
import sair.Pathes;
import sair.sys.SairCons;
import sair.user.Activity;

public class MyActivity extends Activity {

    // 1) Command entry: funcName is the function, args is the raw argument text
    @Override
    public Object main(String funcName, String args) {
        switch (funcName) {
            case "hello":
                SairCons.println("Hello, SairFramework!");
                return true;
            case "greet":
                SairCons.println(FCM.EXECTION_help_Color, "Hello, " + args + "!");
                return true;
            default:
                return false; // returning false makes the framework print help()
        }
    }

    // 2) Help text (one entry per line)
    @Override
    public String[] help() {
        String name = getName();
        return new String[] {
            Pathes.printSplit,
            "MyPlugin v1.0 - my first plugin",
            Pathes.printSplit,
            name + "/hello : print Hello World",
            name + "/greet [name] : greet someone",
        };
    }

    // 3) Exit hook (required; called by /exit or uninstall)
    @Override
    public void exit() {
        SairCons.println("MyPlugin exited");
    }

    // 4) Optional: custom data directory (defaults to the fully-qualified class name)
    @Override
    protected String dataDir() {
        return "myplugin"; // -> data/myplugin/
    }
}
```

**Return value contract** (`main`):

| Return | Framework behavior |
|---|---|
| `null` | Silent, treated as handled |
| `Boolean.FALSE` | Treated as failure; the component's `help()` is printed automatically |
| Anything else | Returned as-is (`ofunc` hands it to `o_funcMain`) |

### 6.3 MANIFEST.MF (ACT)

```text
Manifest-Version: 1.0
ACT: sair.myplugin.MyActivity;
```

- Multiple Activity classes are separated by **semicolons**: `ACT: a.b.Main; a.b.Sub;`
- Missing/empty ACT → red error `ACT_infomations notFound!` on startup and the plugin is skipped;
- Do **not** bundle `SFW.jar` or `SaComS.jar` into your plugin (the framework provides them);
- Export a **plain JAR** (not an executable JAR) containing only your classes and resources.

### 6.4 Lifecycle

1. **Discover**: scan `*.jar` under `plugins/exection/`;
2. **Read**: parse `ACT` from `MANIFEST.MF`;
3. **Load**: create a dedicated `ExectionLoader` and `loadClass`;
4. **Instantiate**: create the Activity via reflection;
5. **Name**: jar file name without extension; duplicates get numeric suffixes;
6. **Register**: store into `Libraries.activities` and `Libraries.exections`;
7. **Run**: receive commands;
8. **Unload**: on `/uninstall`, call `exit()` and `close()`, clean registries, dispose the loader and release the jar handle.

### 6.5 Naming

- Plugin name = **jar file name without `.jar`** (e.g. `myplugin.jar` → `myplugin`);
- Duplicate names get numeric suffixes to stay unique;
- `/rename old new` renames temporarily (lost on restart).

### 6.6 Commands and built-in commands

Every Activity automatically supports these built-ins (dispatched by the framework, no code needed):

`help`, `exit`, `info`, `ofunc`, `close`, `open`, `oset`, `orem`, `uninstall`.

Command format: `plugin/function args`; alias functions with `oset`.

### 6.7 Data directory

Each Activity has its own data directory:

- Default: `data/<fully-qualified class name>/`
- With `dataDir()` overridden: `data/<return value>/`
- Obtain the full path via `getDataDir()` (created on first access)

The framework only concatenates paths; preventing `../` escapes is the plugin's responsibility.

### 6.8 Packaging and deployment

```text
MyPlugin.jar
├─ META-INF/MANIFEST.MF   (contains ACT)
└─ sair/myplugin/*.class
```

- Plugin jar → `plugins/exection/`
- Third-party dependencies → `plugins/lib/`
- Chinese support / shared libs → `plugins/lib/`

Reload by restarting SFW, or run `/load "path/MyPlugin.jar"` in the console.

### 6.9 Dependencies and SPI

- `plugins/lib/` is loaded by the global `SairLoader` and **shared by all plugins**;
- When a plugin command runs, the framework temporarily switches the thread context class loader to that plugin's `ExectionLoader`, so `ServiceLoader`, `DriverManager`, `AudioSystem` and friends can discover `META-INF/services` implementations in `lib`;
- A lib jar may declare `NAME` and `DIR` in its manifest so plugins can obtain its resource directory via `SairLoader.getMOD_MEAT_INFFILE("NAME")` (the `MEAT` typo is historical and cannot be renamed):

```text
Manifest-Version: 1.0
NAME: MyLib;
DIR: sair/res/;
```

### 6.10 Debugging plugins

**Option 1: `Main.toTest` (simplest)**

```java
public static void main(String[] args) {
    Activity acti = new MyActivity();
    Main.toTest(acti, "hello", "");
    Main.toTest(acti, "greet", "Sair");
}
```

**Option 2: register into Libraries to test multi-component scenarios**

```java
public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
    Activity acti = new MyActivity();
    acti.setName("test");
    Libraries.activities.put("test", acti);

    Main.toTest(acti, "", "");            // ensure the framework is initialized
    SairCons.runner(false, "test/hello");
    SairCons.runner(false, "test/greet Sair");
}
```

> `Main.toTest` initializes the framework first (runs the startup flow if needed), then invokes the given function.

### 6.11 Best practices and pitfalls

- Keep `main()` as a dispatcher; delegate real logic to separate classes (the `ActivityAction` pattern);
- Parse path arguments with `ToolPack.pathRepack()` (double-quoted paths);
- Close files, sockets, threads in `exit()`;
- Use `FCM` color constants for visual consistency;
- Avoid special characters in plugin names;
- **`exit()` is mandatory** (compile-time contract);
- On Windows a loaded plugin jar cannot be deleted/overwritten: run `/uninstall` first (the framework releases the handle), otherwise close SFW.

## 7. How the Framework Works

### 7.1 Overall architecture

```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                ConsFrame (Swing console)      │
│   input / IR scripts / plugin output / proxies │
└──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                       │ SairCons.runner(cmd)
                       ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│   SystemSpliter parses: component / function / args │
└──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                       ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Libraries.activities lookup                    │
│   → switch thread context class loader         │
│   → OderFact dispatches built-ins / Activity.main() │
└──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                       ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ plugins (Exection) │ libs (lib → SairLoader)  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 7.2 Startup flow (source view)

`sair.Main.firstLoad()` runs in order:

1. Install the global `SairLoader` as the **thread context class loader** (before any SPI is touched, otherwise codecs/drivers in `lib` are never discovered);
2. Show the console window `ConsFrame.showFrame()`;
3. Check whether the `sairjar:` protocol is available (warn in red and fall back to `jar:` if the factory is taken);
4. Print version and Java environment info;
5. **Load libraries**: serially load every jar in `plugins/lib/` into the global `SairLoader` (a single failure does not abort);
6. **Load plugins**: three-phase pipeline (see 7.5) over `plugins/exection/`;
7. Play the one-shot scanline effect, wait 10 ms;
8. Execute `data/framework/autorun.ir`; if an external `.ir` was passed, run it after autorun finishes;
9. Set `isLoaded = true` (stays false on failure so secondary entry points retry initialization).

Any startup failure is caught, printed in red with a stack trace — the framework never dies silently.

### 7.3 Command pipeline

`SairCons.runner` → `runner0`:

1. Skip blank/comment lines;
2. Handle the SPI uninstall command first;
3. Record command history (max 10000);
4. Parse with `ToolPack.findSplited` (default `SystemSpliter`, replaceable via `SpliterSPI`);
5. Look up the component in `Libraries.activities` (empty name → framework `FrameActivity`);
6. Temporarily switch the thread context class loader to the plugin's `ExectionLoader` (restored afterwards);
7. `OderFact.runner` resolves aliases, dispatches built-ins, otherwise calls `Activity.main(funcName, args)`.

If `main` returns `Boolean.FALSE`, the component's `help()` is printed automatically.

### 7.4 Class-loader hierarchy

```text
System class loader (ClassLoader.getSystemClassLoader())
   └── SairLoader            ← loads plugins/lib/, shared globally
          └── ExectionLoader ← one per plugin, loads plugins/exection/xxx.jar
```

- `SairLoader`: global library loader, parent = system loader; installed as the global thread context loader;
- `ExectionLoader`: per-plugin loader whose parent is `SairLoader`; **one-way visibility** — plugins see lib classes, libs do not see plugin classes, which yields isolation;
- All loaders are `registerAsParallelCapable` and support parallel loading;
- On unload, `dispose()` releases the loader and jar handles (the jar can be deleted/overwritten immediately, even on Windows).

### 7.5 Three-phase plugin loading pipeline (A / B / C)

To shorten startup, `plugins/exection/` loading is split into three phases:

| Phase | Thread | Work |
|---|---|---|
| A | Main thread (directory order) | Open jar, read `ACT`, create `ExectionLoader`; **no class loading** |
| B | Fixed thread pool (CPU cores, clamped to 2–8) | Parallel `loadClass` (pure memory, no constructor side effects) |
| C | Main thread (serial) | Reflectively instantiate, name, register and log; constructor side-effect order matches the legacy behavior |

Failure handling: any failure in B/C unloads that plugin (releasing jar handles and loader), prints a red error, and continues with the rest.

### 7.6 Hot unload

`/uninstall` → `Activity.uninstall()` (final, framework-owned):

1. Locate the owning `Exection` via `Libraries.exections`;
2. Remove from `Libraries.activities` (including aliases);
3. Call `exit()` and `close()` once;
4. `ExectionLoader.dispose()` closes and releases the jar handle;
5. The plugin jar can then be deleted or overwritten (even on Windows).

### 7.7 The `sairjar:` protocol

The JDK's `jar:file:...!/` caches jar handles in the global `JarFileFactory`, keeping files locked after unload. The framework implements a custom `sairjar:` handler:

- Each `openStream` opens and closes its own `JarFile`, with no global cache;
- Used by `findResource` and SPI resource loading;
- If the `URLStreamHandlerFactory` is already taken and registration fails, the framework warns in red and falls back to `jar:` (hot-unload handle release is limited, normal use is unaffected).

### 7.8 IR execution engine

- `IRRunnable` parses a script into a "main sequence + label blocks";
- Only one instance per script name may run at a time (atomic registration in `irpool`);
- Each line reuses the exact manual-input parsing pipeline;
- Supports `/TO:label` recursive jumps (max depth 128) and external `stopIR`;
- Unregisters itself from `irpool` on exit, so startup waits never hang.

### 7.9 Threading model

- The framework **fully dropped EDT scheduling**: startup, command execution and printing run directly on the calling thread;
- Console document mutations are serialized by an internal `ConsFrame` lock;
- Parallelism only happens in Phase B (pure `loadClass`);
- For long tasks use `/newthread [cmd]` or `/ir` (new thread) to avoid blocking the console thread.

### 7.10 Print proxy

```java
public interface PrintRunnable {
    void run(Integer index, java.awt.Color c, String info);
}
```

```java
SairCons.addPrintRunnable("myLogger", new MyLogger()); // register
SairCons.removePrintRunnable("myLogger");              // remove
```

Once registered, every console output passes through the proxy — useful for file logging, remote forwarding, filtering and so on.

### 7.11 SpliterSPI (custom command parser)

```java
public class MySpliterSPI extends sair.user.SpliterSPI {
    @Override
    public sair.sys.tools.Spliter getSpliter(String cmd) {
        return new MySpliter(cmd); // implement getExecName/getExecFunc/getArgs
    }
    @Override
    public String getUninstallCMD() {
        return "/my-spliter-uninstall";
    }
}
```

Compile it into `plugins/lib/`, then run `/setspliter fully.qualified.Class` to install; typing the command returned by `getUninstallCMD()` restores the default parser.

### 7.12 Binary-compatibility constraints

To keep old plugins (from the 0.5.3 era) working, the following are frozen and **must not change**:

- `Main.Version` (name/type/final);
- `Main.main(String[])` and `Main.toTest(Activity, String, String)` signatures;
- `Activity` public final method signatures (close/open/isOpen/getName/setName/alias APIs/getDataDir/uninstall);
- `Libraries.activities/exections/mods` field names and types;
- `LoaderManager.systemLoader/loader/ExecLoaders/libJarPathSet/execJarPathSet`;
- `Pathes` directory fields (`bootDir`/`modDir` were merged into `libDir`, but the fields must remain);
- `IRRunnable.irpool` and the label syntax (`{...}` blocks, `/TO:` jumps).

## 8. Source Layout & Build

This repository contains the **SFW core sources** (the repository does not include a prebuilt `SFW.jar`; see Releases).

### 8.1 Source layout

```text
sairframework/
├─ javacode/               # Java sources (sair.*)
│  └─ sair/
│     ├─ Main.java         # entry point
│     ├─ LoaderManager.java# loading pipeline
│     ├─ SairLoader.java   # global library loader
│     ├─ ExectionLoader.java
│     ├─ SairJarHandler.java # sairjar: protocol
│     ├─ sys/              # console, parsing, IR, GUI, tools
│     └─ user/             # plugin APIs (Activity, PrintRunnable, SpliterSPI)
├─ res/staticfiles/        # embedded resources (logo / font)
├─ bin/                    # Eclipse output dir + runtime dirs (data/plugins)
├─ MANIFEST.MF             # Main-Class: sair.Main
├─ .project / .classpath   # Eclipse project files
├─ readme/                 # static documentation site (index.html + pages/)
└─ newLink.bat             # dev helper: links runtime data/plugins into bin/
```

### 8.2 Build with Eclipse (recommended)

1. `File → Import → Existing Projects into Workspace`, choose the repository root (it ships `.project` / `.classpath`);
2. Source folders are `javacode` and `res`, output folder is `bin`;
3. For runtime debugging, run `newLink.bat` first (it junction-links the live instance's `data`/`plugins` into `bin`);
4. Export: `Export → JAR file`, select `bin/sair` and `bin/staticfiles`, and specify the existing `MANIFEST.MF`.

### 8.3 Build from the command line

Run from the repository root (requires JDK 8+):

```bash
# 1) compile
javac -encoding UTF-8 -source 8 -target 8 -d bin $(find javacode -name "*.java")

# 2) copy embedded resources
cp -r res/staticfiles bin/

# 3) package (only sair/ and staticfiles/; never data/ or plugins/)
jar cfm SFW.jar MANIFEST.MF -C bin sair -C bin staticfiles
```

The resulting `SFW.jar` matches the release artifact and runs directly alongside `plugins/`, `data/`, `run.bat`, etc.

### 8.4 Release

Bundle `SFW.jar`, `run.bat`, `run.sh`, `plugins/` (optionally with sample plugins), `data/framework/` sample scripts and `readme/` into a zip, tag it, and upload it to Gitee Releases.

---

## 9. Compatibility

| Item | Support |
|---|---|
| OS | Windows / Linux / macOS and any Java-capable system |
| Java | Java 8 or newer (JDK 8 recommended for best hot-unload support) |
| Chinese paths/class names | Supported (UTF-8) |
| Legacy plugins | Binary compatible since 0.5.3 (see 7.12) |
| No JRE installed | The release bundles a Windows JRE under `8x64/` |

## 10. FAQ

**Q1: A plugin does not show up.**
- Make sure the jar is in `plugins/exection/`, not `plugins/lib/`;
- Make sure `META-INF/MANIFEST.MF` declares `ACT` with fully qualified class names;
- Check the startup log for red `ACT_infomations notFound!` or `load fail` messages;
- Run `/list` in the console.

**Q2: "xxx is not found".**
- The format is `plugin/function args`; use the name shown by `/list` (defaults to the jar file name).

**Q3: Why does help print after my command returns false?**
- By contract, `main` returning `Boolean.FALSE` means failure, so the framework prints `help()`.

**Q4: The plugin jar cannot be deleted/overwritten.**
- Run `plugin/uninstall` first; the framework releases the jar handle;
- If startup warned about `sairjar` registration failure, the `URLStreamHandlerFactory` was already taken; close SFW to release the file.

**Q5: Double-clicking an IR script does nothing.**
- On Windows, associate `.ir` with `run.bat` first;
- Or run `java -jar SFW.jar "script.ir"`;
- Save scripts as UTF-8 to avoid mojibake.

**Q6: Why does every double-clicked .ir open a new window?**
- SFW is not a singleton; each launch is an independent process (multiple instances can coexist).

**Q7: Where do dependencies go?**
- Always `plugins/lib/`; the global `SairLoader` loads them, with SPI and hot-unload support.

**Q8: How to print colored text from a plugin?**
- `SairCons.println(Color, text)`; color constants live in `sair.FCM`.
